practices.practice: Create a single AsyncMongoClient at application startup and reuse it across the process instead of creating a client per request; Motor is deprecated for new Python async code in favor of PyMongo's AsyncMongoClient.
practices.prior_belief: Create a single Motor client (MotorClient) at app startup and reuse it everywhere (do not create a new client per request); close it on shutdown.

practices.practice: Read the cluster connection string from a secure source at runtime (environment variable such as DOCUMENTDB_URI, Azure Key Vault, or managed identity); do not commit credentials to the repository or logs and provide a .env.example placeholder for local dev.
practices.prior_belief: Read the cluster connection string only from an environment variable (DOCUMENTDB_URI) or from Azure Key Vault / managed identity at runtime; never commit credentials into the repository or logs and provide a .env.example with a placeholder.

practices.practice: Configure the MongoDB async client with TLS and sensible connection-pool and timeout settings (maxPoolSize, minPoolSize, maxIdleTimeMS, connectTimeoutMS, socketTimeoutMS) tuned to your environment (serverless vs long-running), and do not assume Motor is the recommended Python async driver.
practices.prior_belief: Configure the Motor client with TLS enabled and sensible connection-pool settings (maxPoolSize, minPoolSize) appropriate for the orchestrator's concurrency, and reuse the pool across async tasks.

practices.practice: Group multi-operation updates inside a driver session transaction (startSession() + withTransaction / start_transaction) and keep transactions short and idempotent; avoid user interaction while a transaction is open.
practices.prior_belief: Use short, idempotent transactions: perform each orchestrator step and the atomic update in a single MongoDB multi-document transaction via Motor sessions/with_transaction, keep transactions short, and avoid user interaction while a transaction is open.
practices.how_found: Azure DocumentDB transactions best practices (query: "Azure DocumentDB transactions withTransaction keep transactions short")

practices.practice: Use optimistic concurrency in the application (for example a version or lastUpdated field checked in the update predicate) to protect concurrent state updates so a competing updater fails rather than silently overwriting.
practices.prior_belief: Protect concurrent state updates with optimistic concurrency: include a version or lastUpdated timestamp in the query predicate (e.g., findOneAndUpdate where version = X -> version = X+1) so a competing updater fails rather than silently overwriting.
practices.how_found: searched: "Azure DocumentDB optimistic concurrency version findOneAndUpdate"; also looked for service docs describing application-level optimistic concurrency patterns for the Mongo API

practices.practice: Model a state machine document with an embedded, bounded history only when the history is bounded; otherwise store transitions in a separate history collection to avoid unbounded array growth and the 16 MB BSON document limit.
practices.prior_belief: Model the application as a single document with an embedded history array only if the history is bounded; otherwise store transitions in a separate history collection to avoid unbounded array growth and document size limits (MongoDB 16MB limit).

practices.practice: Create a unique index on the application identifier and add a compound index for the orchestrator's primary lookup patterns (e.g., { state: 1, next_run_at: 1 } or { state:1, priority:-1 }) to speed selection of next work items.
practices.prior_belief: Create a unique index on the application identifier (e.g., { application_id: 1 }) and create a compound index for the orchestrator's main lookup patterns (e.g., { state: 1, priority: -1 } or { state: 1, next_run_at: 1 }).
practices.how_found: documentdb-indexing; repository scripts/create_indexes.py demonstrates similar indexes

practices.practice: Use partial or sparse indexes (partialFilterExpression / sparse) for fields that are only present for active items (for example state = 'PENDING') to reduce RU cost and speed queries that select next work items.
practices.prior_belief: Add a partial or sparse index on fields only present for active applications (e.g., partialFilterExpression: { state: 'PENDING' }) to speed selection of next work item and reduce RU/cost for index maintenance.

practices.practice: When storing vectors, use a dedicated vector field with a consistent floating-point format and create the vector index with explicit parameters (dimensions, index type such as DiskANN/HNSW/IVF, and similarity metric like COS/IP/L2) tuned to scale.
practices.prior_belief: When storing vectors, use a dedicated field with a consistent floating-point format (float32 array) and create the vector index with explicit parameters: dimension, indexType (HNSW), M/efConstruction or similar, and metric (cosine/dot/ivf inner product) suitable for your similarity needs.

practices.practice: When combining vector search with metadata filters, push the metadata filters into the same query so prefilters run before the vector search, and project away the vector field when only metadata is required to reduce transfer and RU costs.
practices.prior_belief: When performing vector + metadata filtering, push the metadata filters into the same query so the engine can apply prefilters before the vector search; project away the large vector field when only metadata is required (use projection to exclude vector field).

practices.practice: Handle transient faults with exponential backoff and limited retries (including handling HTTP 429 / rate-limited responses), and design operations to be idempotent where retries are possible.
practices.prior_belief: Use exponential backoff and retry logic for transient errors and rate-limited responses (HTTP 429 for Cosmos DB or equivalent Mongo error codes), limit total retry time, and apply idempotency safeguards for operations retried after partial failure.
practices.how_found: learn.microsoft.com search: "Azure DocumentDB transient faults retry exponential backoff"

practices.practice: Keep transactions and updates small (touch only needed fields); avoid updating large vector blobs inside a transaction to reduce RU consumption, avoid timeouts, and keep transactions short.
practices.prior_belief: Keep transactions and updates small (touch only the fields you need); avoid updating large vector blobs inside a transaction to reduce RU consumption and avoid timeouts.

practices.practice: Use projection to avoid transferring vectors or other large fields unless required, and use batching/pagination when scanning many documents.
practices.prior_belief: Use projection in queries to avoid transferring vectors or other large fields unless required (e.g., collection.find({state:'READY'},{vector:0}) ), and use batch sizes / pagination for loops scanning many docs.

practices.practice: When using Beanie with an async driver, initialize Beanie once at startup with your Motor/Async client and document models and reuse the client for operations (no Azure DocumentDB-specific public guidance found for Beanie; confirm per-project).
practices.prior_belief: When using Beanie with Motor, initialize Beanie once (init_beanie) with the Motor client and document models at startup; reuse the same Motor client for Beanie operations and pass session objects into Beanie/Motor calls when performing transactions.
practices.how_found: searched: "Beanie init_beanie Azure DocumentDB Motor AsyncMongoClient guidance"; repository uses Beanie but no Azure DocumentDB public doc specifically about Beanie

practices.practice: Record audited state transitions (actor, timestamp, previous_state, next_state, metadata) and make the append part of the same atomic update/transaction so the transition is never lost.
practices.prior_belief: Record audited state transitions in the document (actor, timestamp, previous_state, next_state, metadata) and make this append operation part of the same atomic update or transaction so the document never loses the transition record.
practices.source_name: Group multiple operations in transactions in Azure DocumentDB
practices.how_found: learn.microsoft.com search: "Azure DocumentDB transactions atomic update audit history"

practices.practice: Be cautious with long-lived change streams in production: enabling pre-images increases storage and processing overhead and continuous pre-image enablement is discouraged unless explicitly required.
practices.prior_belief: Avoid long-lived change streams or tailable cursors for orchestration unless you validate the Mongo compatibility and performance for the managed service; instead use polling/cron with indexed queries for next work item selection.
practices.how_found: learn.microsoft.com search: "Azure DocumentDB change streams pre-images overhead"

practices.practice: Create indexes (including vector indexes) before bulk-loading or running large backfills; vector index creation can be expensive—create indexes once then load data to avoid repeated reindex cost.
practices.prior_belief: Provision indexes before bulk-loading or running large backfills; creating vector indexes can be expensive—create them once and then load data to avoid repeated reindex cost.

practices.practice: Limit the size of embedded history writes with $push + $slice or cap the history length (e.g., $push: { history: { $each:[entry], $position:0, $slice:100 } }) to prevent unbounded document growth.
practices.prior_belief: Limit the size of embedded history array writes with $push + $slice or use capped history length (e.g., $push: { history: { $each:[entry], $position:0, $slice:100 } }) to prevent unbounded growth inside the document.

practices.practice: In CI, mock the DB and driver sessions for unit tests and run integration tests that seed and mutate a live cluster only when permitted by policy; keep fast unit tests isolated from slow live-cluster tests.
practices.prior_belief: Design unit tests to mock the DB and Motor sessions for fast CI runs; separate integration tests that actually seed and mutate the live cluster and run those only when explicitly allowed.
practices.how_found: searched: "unit tests mock Motor Beanie Azure DocumentDB guidance"; repository tests use mocks (tests/test_orchestrator.py)

practices.practice: Monitor RU/throughput and slow queries using the provider's diagnostic tools (enable diagnostic settings, analyze slow-query logs in Log Analytics), use explain() to diagnose slow queries, and alert on RU throttling (HTTP 429).
practices.prior_belief: Monitor RU/throughput and slow query plans using the provider's tools; add indexes for slow filters/sorts (use explain() in the documentdb MCP tools) and set alerts for RU throttling (429s).
practices.how_found: documentdb-monitoring; learn.microsoft.com search: "Azure DocumentDB monitor RU throttling slow queries"

practices.practice: When using transactions, implement recommended retry-on-transient-failure logic (retry the withTransaction callback on transient errors) and ensure the transaction body is idempotent.
practices.prior_belief: When using transactions, implement retry-on-transient-failure logic recommended for MongoDB transactions (retry the entire with_transaction callable when encountering transient errors or UnknownTransactionCommitResult), and ensure idempotency of the transaction body.
practices.how_found: learn.microsoft.com search: "Azure DocumentDB transactions retry withTransaction"

practices.practice: Keep per-document size well under the 16 MB limit by avoiding large inline blobs or very high-dimension vectors; store large payloads in external object storage (Azure Blob) and keep references in documents.
practices.prior_belief: Keep per-document size under MongoDB limits by avoiding storing large file blobs or high-dimension vectors inline if they will push document size up; consider external object storage (Blob) for large payloads with references in documents.

practices.practice: Use explain('executionStats') to verify index usage (keysExamined / docsExamined) and avoid COLLSCAN in production queries.
Enable in-region high availability (HA) on production clusters to get 99.99% SLA and automatic failover; add cross-region replica for higher SLA and cross-region DR when needed.

Harden production clusters with network isolation (Private Endpoint / firewall rules), prefer Microsoft Entra ID + RBAC for authentication, and use customer-managed keys (CMK) for data-at-rest encryption where required.

Where an installed skill provided authoritative Azure-DocumentDB-specific guidance I used it (source_kind=installed_skill). Prior beliefs were then checked against the public record: K01 and K03 are contradicted in that Azure guidance recommends PyMongo's AsyncMongoClient for new Python async code rather than Motor, but the singleton-client and pool/timeout recommendations hold; K05, K14 and K19 had no Azure-DocumentDB public source and are marked prior_knowledge_only; all other prior beliefs were found and marked confirmed. The repository's README and scripts show patterns consistent with many of these practices (DOCUMENTDB_URI env var, index scripts, use of transactions, and tests that use mocks).
